lesson_title: Four People, Eight Towers, One Brief
hook_text: Your tower sketch is about to be judged by three classmates. Here is how that makes it better instead of worse.
clip_script: Four learners, two tower sketches each, one shared brief. Specifications down the side of a table, sketches across the top. Tall enough? Tick. Base inside 150? Question mark, it is drawn at 170. Rigid? Cross: thin single diagonals up top and nothing inside, so it will twist. Every mark gets a reason in the words of the term, never I do not like it. Two lists under each tower: what is good, what is weak, at least two of each. Then the rules. Talk about the design, not the person. Say what works first. Point to the brief. Suggest, do not order. And when it is your turn to listen: hear it all, write it down, ask a question, say thanks, decide later. Then go back to your own page and change things, one comment at a time, each with a reason. Draw the improved tower beside the old one. Never rub out the original. The design got better because more eyes looked at it. That is the process working.
visual_style: Whiteboard table filling with ticks, crosses and question marks under two tower sketches; speech bubbles with design-not-designer phrasing; a third improved sketch appears beside the originals.
mood: Supportive and businesslike, criticism made safe and useful.
pacing: Table fills quickly, rules land one per beat, calm close on the before-and-after sketches.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and evaluate a classmate's sketch using the table and the rules.
